transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… since my daughter left for basic training, I haven’t been handling things right. The house feels empty when I get home. I’ve been crying before work, messing up steps on jobs I’ve done for years, snapping at people. I don’t really do the things I used to—going out on the water, working on my sculpture. Just… don’t see much point lately.
How long have you been feeling this way since your daughter left for basic training?
About a month. Pretty much since she left, I’ve been… like this.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Not really. I used to like going out on the water, or working on my sculpture, but… since she left, I just come home and the house feels dead. I don’t really see the point in doing any of it right now.
Do you feel guilty about anything related to your daughter leaving for basic training?
I don’t know… not exactly guilty. I just keep turning it over in my head, but I’m not sure what I’m supposed to feel bad about.
Are there any small things that still give you pleasure, like a favorite food or a beautiful sunset?

Not really. Maybe for a second I’ll notice something, but it doesn’t stick. I mostly just come home and the house feels… dead. I don’t go out on the water or work on my sculpture anymore. I just don’t see the point right now.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself since your daughter left for basic training?
I… I don’t really want to get into that. I haven’t made any kind of plan or anything, if that’s what you mean.
Have you noticed any change in your weight since your daughter left for basic training?
I haven’t really checked. My clothes feel about the same, I guess… I haven’t noticed much.
Can you tell me more about what you meant when you said you didn't want to get into thoughts of hurting yourself?

I just meant… it’s hard to talk about. I don’t really have the words for it, and I don’t like saying that kind of thing out loud. I’m not trying to be difficult. I just… don’t want to go there right now.
Have you had thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself or end your life since your daughter left?
I… I don’t know. I don’t really want to talk about that. It’s just… not something I can get into right now.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but no longer find pleasure in?

Yeah… I guess so. I used to go out on the water, or mess around with this sculpture I was working on. Since my daughter left, I just… don’t really see the point. I come home and the house feels dead, and I mostly just sit there.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I have. I used to like going out on the water, and I had this sculpture I was working on. Since my daughter left, I just… don’t care about it. I get home and the house feels empty, and I just sit there. I don’t really see the point.
Do you feel like your low mood is present most of the day?

Yeah… most of it, I guess. Since my daughter left, it’s like I come home and the whole place feels dead. I try to hold it together, but even before work I’ll be sitting in the truck crying. It doesn’t really let up much.
Do you feel like your low mood is interfering with your ability to work or take care of things at home?

Yeah… it is. Work’s been harder. My supervisor actually pulled me off this more complicated welding job because I wasn’t… keeping things coordinated safely enough.

And at home, I’ve just let things slide. I had a sculpture submission I was supposed to finish, and I just… didn’t. The deadline passed.
Do you feel like your low mood is present nearly every day?

Yeah. Pretty much every day since my daughter left for basic. I come home and the house just feels… dead. I try to keep it together, but I’m crying before shifts sometimes, and I don’t really feel like doing anything I used to.
How many days a week would you say you've been feeling this low mood since your daughter left?
Pretty much every day. I mean… maybe there’s a few hours here and there where I’m busy enough not to think about it, but since she left, it’s been most days of the week. Like six or seven, I guess.
Would you say your low mood is mild, moderate, or severe?

Severe, I guess. I don’t like saying that, but… since my daughter left, I’m crying before shifts, messing up work I’ve done for years, and I’ve stopped doing the stuff I usually care about. It feels pretty bad.
